source: The first study to successfully characterize enhancer activity using CRISPR/Cas9 studied the human erythroid enhancer of BCL11A (Canver et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Canver et al., 2015.

claim: BCL11A is a developmentally crucial transcriptional repressor that facilitates fetal (HbF) to adult hemoglobin switching.
source: BCL11A is a developmentally crucial transcriptional repressor that facilitates fetal (HbF) to adult hemoglobin switching (Bauer et al., 2012).

claim: Bauer et al. identified common genetic variants in the erythroid-specific enhancer of BCL11A that was associated with HbF expression.
source: Bauer et al identified common genetic variants in the erythroid-specific enhancer of BCL11A that was associated with HbF expression (Bauer et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bauer et al., 2013.

claim: Canver et al. pinpointed nucleotides in the BCL11A enhancer that altered BCL11A expression and subsequently HbF expression by dissecting the enhancer at near-base-pair resolution using CRISPR/Cas9 saturation mutagenesis.
source: By dissecting the enhancer at near-base-pair resolution using CRISPR/Cas9 saturation mutagenesis, the authors pinpointed nucleotides in the enhancer that altered BCL11A expression and subsequently HbF expression (Canver et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Canver et al., 2015.

claim: Canver et al. tiled the BCL11A enhancers identified using DNAse hypersensitivity assays with gRNAs and quantified the effect of perturbation on target gene HbF through flow cytometry-based sorting.
source: Specifically, the authors tiled the enhancers identified using DNAse hypersensitivity assays with gRNAs and quantified the effect of perturbation on target gene HbF, through flow cytometry-based sorting.
evidence: Stated as a methodological approach from Canver et al.'s study.

claim: Double-strand breaks caused by CRISPR/Cas9 can be detrimental to cells.
source: One drawback of CRISPR/Cas9 approaches is that the double-strand breaks caused can be detrimental to the cells.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of CRISPR/Cas9.

claim: Base editing has solved the problem of detrimental double-strand breaks caused by CRISPR/Cas9.
source: Recently developed technologies like base editing have solved this problem.

claim: Martin-Rufino et al. applied base editing screens to precisely alter variants in the promoter region of the γ-hemoglobin gene (HBG1/2).

claim: Martin-Rufino et al. identified new and previously known variants that increase HbF expression using a pooled base editing screen for ~120 sgRNAs targeting the 300 bp promoter, coupled with FACS-based enrichment for HbF populations.
source: Using a pooled base editing screen for ~120 sgRNAs targeting the 300 bp promoter, coupled with FACS-based enrichment for HbF populations, the authors identified new and previously known variants that increase HbF expression.
evidence: Stated as a finding from Martin-Rufino et al.'s study.

claim: Martin-Rufino et al. performed pooled single-cell genotyping to link the nucleotide variants to the phenotype.
source: Importantly, the authors also performed pooled single-cell genotyping to link the nucleotide variants to the phenotype.
evidence: Stated as a methodological approach from Martin-Rufino et al.'s study.

claim: Chen et al. took a tiered approach by combining deep learning-based methodologies with CRISPRi and base editing screens to identify variants in enhancers of CD69.
source: In a separate study, Chen et al., took a tiered approach by combining deep learning-based methodologies with CRISPRi and base editing screens to identify variants in enhancers of CD69 (Chen et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2023.

claim: Morris et al. extended base editing screening strategy to functionally test GWAS variants for blood traits with a single-cell RNA-Seq readout.
source: Finally, Morris et al., extended this base editing screening strategy to functionally test GWAS variants for blood traits with a single-cell RNA-Seq readout (Morris et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Morris et al., 2023.

claim: Prime editing can be applied to study enhancer variants.
source: Besides base editing, other methods like prime editing, which is currently being used to study variants in protein-coding regions, can be also applied to study enhancer variants (Erwood et al., 2022).

claim: Findlay et al. used saturation mutagenesis to study 13 exons of BRCA1 to characterize variants of unknown significance.
source: Findlay et al., used saturation mutagenesis to study 13 exons of BRCA1 to characterize variants of unknown significance (Findlay et al., 2018).

claim: Findlay et al. used homology-directed repair to supply all possible single nucleotide variants and quantified the effects using growth-based screens.
source: This study used homology-directed repair to supply all possible single nucleotide variants and quantified the effects using growth-based screens.
evidence: Stated as a methodological approach from Findlay et al.'s study.

claim: Findlay et al. sequenced the installed variants in genomic DNA and measured the effects of the variants at the RNA level.
source: Since the authors sequenced the installed variants in genomic DNA and measured the effects of the variants at the RNA level, this study offers a comprehensive way to link variants to gene expression.

claim: ~90% of disease-associated variants are non-coding and likely at enhancers according to GWAS.

claim: The vast majority of enhancers and their phenotype-associated genetic variants remain uncharacterized.
source: However, to date, the vast majority of enhancers and their phenotype-associated genetic variants remain uncharacterized.

claim: Existing enhancer studies have largely focused on static in vitro systems, especially immortalized or primary cell lines.
source: Existing enhancer studies have largely focused on static in vitro systems, especially immortalized or primary cell lines (Fulco et al., 2019).

claim: CRISPRi studies have been performed in human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) during differentiation.

claim: Understanding how enhancers work together to establish and maintain gene expression networks could require a dense sampling of time points.

claim: Organoids are currently available for a variety of developmental systems including the brain, kidney, and heart.

claim: A CRISPRi screen has been applied to an organoid model, identifying key TFs in fetal lung development through perturbation of select promoters.
source: A CRISPRi screen has been applied to an organoid model, identifying key TFs in fetal lung development through perturbation of select promoters (Sun et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sun et al., 2022.

claim: In vivo systems are currently able to interrogate individual enhancers and variants.
source: In vivo systems are currently able to interrogate individual enhancers and variants (Smemo et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Smemo et al., 2012.

claim: In vivo CRISPR screens have been accomplished.
source: While in vivo CRISPR screens have been accomplished, perturbation complexity remains a key challenge (Gemberling et al., 2021; Jin et al., 2020).

claim: FISH-based methods have been adapted to identify regulatory elements of key genes by perturbing enhancers and sorting cells based on fluorescence intensity after RNA labeling.

claim: FISH-based approaches can only survey a handful of pre-identified genes.
source: One drawback is that FISH-based approaches can only survey a handful of pre-identified genes.

claim: MerFISH, seqFISH, osmFISH, and others can increase the scale of genes detected.
source: More recent approaches including MerFISH, seqFISH, osmFISH, and others can increase the scale of genes detected, but are significantly more challenging to establish (Codeluppi et al., 2018; De Biase et al., 2021; Eng et al., 2019; Xia et al., 2019).

claim: Targeted transcript amplification has been developed to enrich genes of interest.
source: Similarly, targeted transcript amplification has been developed to enrich genes of interest (Schraivogel et al., 2020).

claim: Cell Painting is a multiplexed image-based assay for the detection of cellular organelles like mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and cytoskeleton through fluorescent dyes.
source: For example, Cell Painting is a multiplexed image-based assay for the detection of cellular organelles like mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and cytoskeleton through fluorescent dyes (Bray et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bray et al., 2016.

claim: Optical screens in combination with CRISPR perturbations can provide information on organelle localization, cell morphology, and cell-cell interactions.
source: In combination with CRISPR perturbations, optical screens can provide information on organelle localization, cell morphology, and cell-cell interactions (Feldman et al., 2019).

claim: Optical CRISPR screens have been employed to characterize multiple phenotypic features of perturbation of essential genes.

evidence: Supported by citation to Funk et al., 2022.

claim: Cunningham et al. identified two enhancers of Tbx5 that are not essential for limb development through genetic knockout.
source: For example, Cunningham et al., identified two enhancers of Tbx5 that are not essential for limb development through genetic knockout (Cunningham et al., 2018).

claim: It is not feasible to experimentally test all regulatory elements and sequence variants for their impact on developmental disorders.
source: Since there are millions of regulatory elements in the human genome and many more sequence variants, it is not feasible to experimentally test all of them for their impact on developmental disorders.

claim: Computational models that can accurately predict the regulatory activity of sequence variants will be an essential component to close the gap in understanding enhancer function.
source: Computational models that can accurately predict the regulatory activity of sequence variants will be an essential component to close this gap.
evidence: Stated as a future need.

claim: Sei is a sequence-based deep learning model trained on a compendium of ~20,000 epigenetic features, including open chromatin and transcription factor binding from ~1300 cell lines and tissues.
source: For example, Sei is a sequence-based deep learning model trained on a compendium of ~20,000 epigenetic features, including open chromatin and transcription factor binding from ~1300 cell lines and tissues (Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2022.

claim: Sei accurately predicts whether a DNA sequence is a regulatory element and in what cell contexts.
source: Given a DNA sequence, Sei accurately predicts whether the sequence is a regulatory element and in what cell contexts.

claim: Sei can predict how genetic variants alter enhancer activity.
source: Since Sei models sequences, it can also predict how genetic variants alter enhancer activity.

claim: Enformer applies deep learning to predict gene regulatory activity from genomic sequences.
source: Similarly, Enformer also applies deep learning to predict gene regulatory activity from genomic sequences (Avsec et al., 2021).

claim: Enformer can use information from distal genomic interactions (~100 kb) to improve predictions.

claim: Enformer can predict long-range interactions between promoters and enhancers.
source: In this way, Enformer can predict long-range interactions between promoters and enhancers.

claim: Current predictive modeling approaches have focused on predicting molecular phenotypes including expression and epigenetic status.
source: First, current approaches have focused on predicting molecular phenotypes including expression and epigenetic status.

claim: Accurate predictions of enhancer function rely on good training data.
source: Second, accurate predictions rely on good training data.

claim: Much of existing training data for predictive models is derived from cell lines.
source: However, much of our existing training data is derived from cell lines.
evidence: Stated as a current limitation.

claim: Epigenetic data from human developmental systems, especially in vivo, are still rare.
source: Epigenetic data from human developmental systems, especially in vivo, are still rare.
evidence: Stated as a current limitation.

source: Active learning strategies with deep integration of experimental and modeling components will be crucial to guide experiments to where computational modeling can be most improved.
evidence: Stated as a future need.

claim: Predictive models need to be accurate across diverse populations, which requires the ability to model the effect of genetic background.
source: Third, predictive models need to be accurate across diverse populations, and doing so requires the ability to model the effect of genetic background.

claim: The development of explainable AI models will offer insights into these models and the features important for prediction.

claim: Improved predictive modeling capabilities will drive clinical applications to interpret the molecular, cellular, and organismal impact of newly identified variants in patients.
source: We anticipate that improved predictive modeling capabilities will drive clinical applications to interpret the molecular, cellular, and organismal impact of newly identified variants in patients.

source: The 2010s witnessed the comprehensive mapping of enhancers, as well as new genome engineering tools to perturb enhancers endogenously at scale, both at increasingly cellular resolution.

source: In the coming decade, we anticipate that innovative technologies will spearhead the high-throughput characterization of how developmental enhancers and their genetic variants impact molecular and cellular phenotypes in vivo (Figure 2).

claim: Experimental strategies alone will not be sufficient to gain comprehensive views of all enhancers at the nucleotide and cellular resolution.
source: However, to gain comprehensive views of all enhancers at the nucleotide and cellular resolution, experimental strategies alone will not be sufficient.

claim: Predictive modeling and machine learning approaches will be instrumental to achieve comprehensive views of all enhancers at the nucleotide and cellular resolution.
source: Predictive modeling and machine learning approaches will be instrumental to achieve this goal.

source: Ultimately, this knowledge will enable the interpretation of enhancer variants in both research and clinical settings.

source: The functional characterization of enhancer variants is a multi-step process linking genotypes to molecular phenotypes (target genes and networks), cellular phenotypes (cell state, morphology), and organismal phenotypes (developmental defect) (top row).
